newsitem.title: KENYA: Improved demand pushes Nairobi bourse index.
newsitem.headline: Improved demand pushes Nairobi bourse index.

text.p: Improved demand for key shares helped sustain bullish sentiment of the Nairobi Stock Exchange on Thursday, brokers and bourse officials said.
The 20-share index gained 8.22 points to stand at 3032.62.
Turnover dropped to 6.280 million shillings traded on 198,166 shares versus 35.394 million shillings on Wednesday.
Uchumi Supermarket and Kenya Commercial Bank remained the most actively traded shares in the market and registered marginal price gains.

On average, prices were steady to firm across the board. Uchumi traded at 44.50 from 44, Kenya Commercial Bank traded at 60 from 59, Bamburi Cement gained 25 cents to close at 28.25, while Kenya Breweries gained 1.0 to close at 51.
A broker said there was improved demand from both local investors and foreigners in Kenya Commercial Bank which helped keep the bank's price on the rise.
"We are very happy when there are big deals in the market. It means a lot of orders are coming in," he added.
The market's mood seemed to be picking up. Brokers said they had been very worried when the index went below the 2000-point level last Friday.
"We were very worried, all we were doing is look at one another," one broker said.

There was an air of excitement in the market as the bourse prepared for it's first day of trading in corporate bonds -- on December 2. "Things look very good, there is a lot of interest in the market," a broker said.
"We even expect it to get better next year when they begin trading treasury bills in the market," a senior broker said.

He said the raising of the minimum investment on treasury bills to 1.0 million shillings by the Central Bank of Kenya would ensure that small investors looked for an alternative secondary market, in this case the Nairobi Stock Exchange.
Oil concern Total Kenya traded at 63 unchanged.
The regulatory Capital Markets Authority (CMA) on Wednesday announced the resumption of trading of Kenya Oil Company shares on the bourse, effective December 16.
Kenol was suspended mid this year after it told the CMA that it wanted to be delisted from the bourse.

CMA chief executive Paul Melly said the lifting of the suspension was an important development necessary to ensure maintenance of investor confidence, protection of minority investors, as well as liquidity, critical for sustainable development of an orderly, fair and efficient capital markets.
Kenya Airways traded 37,658 shares unchanged at 8.90.
